A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3D-RFT work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection, grounding, and spatial-reasoning results, alongside ablations, training curves, and qualitative examples in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds grounding error-distribution analysis and evaluations across additional benchmarks and model scales.

M1.justification: The SFT-to-GRPO pipeline, original model components, task-specific rewards, and loss chunking remain unchanged. The added 8B evaluation documents a model-scale extension, without establishing a new algorithm or architectural component.

E1.justification: Appendix B.1 substantially broadens spatial-reasoning evaluation with MMSI-Bench, All-Angles, and ERQA, using sparse multi-image inputs. It also adds RFT evaluations labeled MindCube; the earlier MindCube-Tiny SFT analysis remains present, so that dataset family is not entirely new.

E2.justification: New Table 5 adds VST-7B as a comparator. Its VST-3B row corresponds to the existing VST-RL-3B comparison, including the same 57.7 VSI-Bench score. Comparator membership in Tables 1–4 is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1 adds evaluation of an 8B configuration alongside 4B and describes few-image inputs for the additional benchmarks. Existing experimental settings and metrics are retained; the new statement that VSI-Bench uses 32 frames does not establish a changed earlier protocol.

E4.justification: Section 4.4.2 and Figure 9 add an error-distribution analysis testing whether RFT reduces zero-overlap grounding failures. Appendix B.1 also investigates model-scale sensitivity across benchmarks, including reversed scaling on MMSI-Bench. These substantially extend the existing training-strategy, data-quality, and training-dynamics analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeat counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing training-curve reporting is unchanged. The new IoU density plot analyzes prediction errors rather than introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their results. New Table 5 adds benchmark and model-scale results: the 8B model scores 64.0 on VSI-Bench versus the retained 4B score of 62.8, while newly reported MMSI-Bench scores are 28.0 and 29.9, respectively. These are different configurations, not revised 4B performance. Figure 9 additionally reports reduced zero-overlap grounding errors.

T1.justification: Equations 1–16 and the mathematical formulations remain unchanged. Despite its 'Theoretical Analysis' heading, new Section 4.4.1 and Figure 8 provide a conceptual illustration of one-hot supervision versus geometric rewards, without adding formal assumptions, derivations, proofs, or counterexamples.

C1.justification: The abstract changes 'the first framework' to 'a systematic framework,' withdrawing an explicit priority claim. The central contributions and claims about metric-aligned training and 4B model effectiveness remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 adds an explanation contrasting SFT's zero-overlap failures with RFT's more localized errors. Appendix B.1 attributes MMSI-Bench weaknesses and reversed scaling to limited training-data diversity. Existing limitations concerning task-specific training and missing perception CoT data are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 newly specifies 32-frame VSI-Bench inputs and describes the other benchmark inputs as several images. Appendix A's hardware, fine-tuning choices, and chunk sizes are unchanged, as is project-page access. Detailed implementation information for the added 8B experiments is not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for MMSI-Bench, All-Angles, and Chen et al.'s 2026 work on lifting unlabeled data for 3D understanding. It also explicitly positions the already-cited VST as concurrent generalist work and distinguishes 3D-RFT's focus on video-based RLVR.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and related-work discussion receive localized revisions, with new Sections 4.4 and B.1. Appendix subsections are renumbered, the limitations text moves before the qualitative figures, and the publication header changes. The overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the conceptual reward-surface illustration, IoU density plot, and Table 5. Existing figures retain their image content, with appendix Figures 8–14 becoming Figures 10–16. Table 4 and appendix material are repositioned, and grounding-example labels are restyled.

improvement.justification: The added evaluations make generalization and scaling limits more visible, including the MMSI-Bench weakness, while the ScanRefer error analysis supplies evidence beyond aggregate scores. Removing the priority claim also improves positioning. These are useful but bounded gains: the added evaluations remain sparsely documented, and the optimization explanation is conceptual rather than a formal demonstration.
